Build Caravansary
Caravansary: resupply next turn
Nearby Caravansary is inactive: needs an intact road to one of your cities.

A worker-built outpost requiring Engineering and a Ministry of Coin in your empire. Select a worker and use Build Caravansary; construction continues automatically each turn, using its movement, until complete. Moving or giving another construction order cancels it. Losing the Ministry pauses it. Spend a turn on it or one adjacent land tile to clear all environmental exposure and penalties. The Caravansary must belong to you and have an unbroken road or railroad, including on its own tile, to any city you own. Roads may cross your territory, unclaimed land, or a trade agreement partner's territory. Pillaging, gaps, and enemy occupation break supply. A city needs no separate road on its center tile. An outpost outside borders belongs to its builder; inside borders it belongs to the tile owner. Does not restore lost HP. Military relief is for your units; authorized partner caravans may use the outpost. Build time matches a Fort. Existing outposts still operate if the Ministry is lost.

Caravansaries provide water, shelter, and medical supplies for expeditions. A Ministry of Coin authorizes their construction throughout the empire after Engineering, including on unclaimed land. They use fort graphics without a defensive bonus. Their supply route must be maintained: a disconnected outpost gives no environmental relief. Existing home-territory protection remains automatic.
Ministry of Coin

National Wonder: one per player. Increases land trade route range by 50% and adds 2 [ICON_GOLD] Gold to international land trade routes originating in this city. Unlocks worker-built Caravansary improvements throughout your empire after Engineering. No maintenance. Base cost: 125 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production, increasing with the number of cities. Cannot be purchased or captured. No prerequisite building is required in every city.

Build the Ministry of Coin in a land trade hub to gain the former city Caravansary's trade benefits. Your workers can then construct Caravansary outposts after Engineering. Connect these outposts to your cities with roads to support armies beyond your borders. Losing the Ministry prevents further outpost construction until it is rebuilt, but existing outposts continue operating.

The Ministry of Coin oversees commerce and the establishment of roadside Caravansaries. It replaces the former city Caravansary as a national institution, combining local trade benefits with authority to construct an empire-wide network of outposts.

Exposure is checked at the start of your turn, before you move, for the tile occupied overnight. Desert: 2 safe turns. Tundra: 3. Snow: 1. Jungle: 4. The next two excess turns cause strain; further exposure causes exhaustion. Safe ground removes 2 exposure per turn. Your own borders reset all exposure immediately. An accessible oasis on this tile or one tile away, an adjacent lake, a river on this tile, or flood plains clear heat after a turn. Coasts do not. Different climate penalties never stack; changing hostile climates retains previous exposure. Embarkation pauses counters and land penalties.

Support: scouts gain 2 grace turns; forested tundra accumulates half as quickly; Engineering adds 1 cold grace turn; Biology adds 1 jungle grace turn; Penicillin adds another 2. A same-team Medic I or II on this tile or an adjacent land tile adds 2 jungle grace turns. Bonuses stack, but multiple medics do not. Civilians, ships, aircraft, and barbarians are exempt. AI and human armies use the same rules.

Cancel construction

Establish a land route through the Trade and logistics planner while in one of your cities. International trade requires agreements. Active caravans are simulated by the mod and listed in its planner. The unit returns after completion or recall; a lost caravan is destroyed. Remains available after Combustion as the cheaper alternative to a Motorized Caravan. Existing Caravans do not upgrade or become obsolete.
Motorized Caravan

Optional land trader unlocked by Combustion. Costs 150 [ICON_PRODUCTION] Production and uses one trade slot while operating. Does not replace the ordinary Caravan. Crosses all passable land without roads or Caravan Logistics and ignores Desert, Tundra, Snow and Jungle exposure, relief penalties and terrain movement costs. Gold is reduced by 40% without continuous roads and another 40% without a supplied Caravansary stop: 20% with neither, 60% with one, 100% with both. These deductions do not affect domestic food or production. Mountains, ice and water still block land routes. Trade agreements, range limits and raids still apply. Use Trade and logistics to establish routes.

Build a Motorized Caravan for reliable access across undeveloped land. Keep ordinary Caravans for cheaper trade on established corridors; both units remain available. Roadless travel and missing Caravansary service reduce gold, even on mild terrain. A service stop must be on the route, intact, authorized and connected by roads to its owner's city. Adjacent relief, an oasis, and being inside your borders do not substitute for a commercial stop. Roads still extend range and station garrisons still protect road traffic. No strategic resource is required.

Motorized convoys carry cargo, repair equipment and supplies across undeveloped land. Their self-sufficiency removes environmental exposure and relief requirements, while commercial depots and roads keep transport profitable. This is an alternative to the ordinary Caravan, not its replacement or upgrade. Combustion unlocks production without changing existing units or routes. A supplied Caravansary stop and continuous roads each remove a 40% gold deduction, regardless of terrain. The planner seeks a reachable station detour when it improves gold efficiency; active routes retain their chosen path. Saves preserve unit identity, and completion or recall returns the same type. This alpha reuses the standard Caravan model, flag and portrait pending dedicated vehicle artwork.

Establish a sea route through the Trade and logistics planner while in one of your coastal cities. International trade requires agreements. Active ships are simulated by the mod; native trade controls are replaced.
Caravan Logistics
Allows Caravans to cross roadless unclaimed territory. Missing roads and harsh-terrain relief still reduce trade payments by 40% each. Requires Engineering.

Organized transport, reserve supplies, and navigation enable caravans to cross undeveloped land without a continuous road. Before this technology, a caravan entering roadless unclaimed land is lost. Foreign territory still requires a trade agreement.
A distant market rewards those who prepare the journey.
Sheltered in Resource Outpost
Irrigation Works

Unlocks worker construction of Irrigated Farms on flat Desert tiles assigned to this city. Each new farm needs a continuous path through your intact irrigated farms to a mountain, river, lake or oasis. Requires Engineering. 1 [ICON_GOLD] maintenance.
Build in a desert city with access to water or mountain runoff. Start farms at a source and extend the network outward. Protect and repair the connecting farms to keep downstream land productive.

Irrigation works coordinate channels and water distribution to cultivate arid land. This city's workers may build connected irrigated farms. Selling or losing the building stops new construction in its assigned territory; existing farms continue to work while connected to water.
Irrigated Farm
Irrigated Farm (dry)
Build Irrigated Farm

Flat Desert only, including Flood Plains and Wheat. Requires Engineering and Irrigation Works in the city assigned this tile. Replaces an ordinary farm or uses unimproved land. Connected: +3 [ICON_FOOD] from the improvement. Disconnected: +1 [ICON_FOOD]. Normal farm Civil Service/Fertilizer bonuses also apply. A river on the tile or an adjacent mountain, lake or oasis supplies water. Water travels only through intact irrigated farms belonging to you; ordinary farms, cities, foreign farms and coasts do not carry water. Pillage or capture can cut downstream supply; repair or an alternative connected path restores it. Food states reconcile at turn boundaries and after construction/repair; the status line checks live connectivity.

Workers extend a network of channels from natural water sources into desert farmland. A closed loop without a source cannot supply itself. Disconnecting water leaves the farm intact at ordinary farm yields, and reconnecting restores the irrigation bonus automatically. Pillaged farms neither yield food nor carry water. Farm graphics are reused for both supplied and dry land.

Requires owned flat Desert, unimproved or an ordinary farm. Flood Plains and Wheat are allowed; other features, visible resources and improvements are not. Repair existing irrigated farms with the normal Repair action.
The city assigned this tile needs Irrigation Works. Reassign an overlapping tile in the city screen if necessary.
No continuous water connection. Start beside a mountain, lake or oasis, or on a river, then extend through your intact irrigated farms. A broken connection pauses construction.
Water connection available. Start construction once to work automatically each turn. Moving, another order or Cancel ends the assignment.
Water connected: +2 food bonus
No water: ordinary farm yields
Pillaged: repair to carry water
